name: Assam

communities.name: Hindu
communities.notes: Mostly Vaishnava; satras and namghars are central institutions. Mekhela chador for women, dhoti/kurta and gamosa for men; gamosa used by everyone, across religions.

communities.name: Muslim
communities.notes: About 40 lakh Assamese-speaking Muslims, recognised as indigenous Assamese Muslims in 2022. Men wear kurta and lungi with a gamosa; women wear the mekhela sador adapted for modesty. Celebrate Bihu as well as Eid; zikir and zari devotional songs (from the 17th-century saint Azan Faqir) are part of Assamese culture.

communities.name: Muslim
communities.notes: Bengali-speaking Muslim community, distinct from Assamese Muslims. Dress still to research; depict neutrally in everyday life (see avoid list).

communities.name: Hindu
communities.notes: Majority in the Barak Valley. Dress still to research.

communities.name: Bodo
communities.notes: Women: dokhona with colourful woven floral designs. Men: gamsa tied at the waist. Aronai scarf for honour and winter.

communities.name: Mising
communities.notes: River-valley community of Upper Assam. Women: ege (lower wrap) with gero; men: white mibu galuk shirt, damur cloth. Ali-Aye-Ligang sowing festival.

communities.name: Karbi
communities.notes: Hill community of Karbi Anglong. Textiles: pini (women's lower garment), vamkok (women's girdle), pekok, seleng, jiso khonjari, jirik; a GI tag is being sought. Full outfits not yet sourced.

communities.name: Rabha
communities.notes: Lower Assam (e.g. Goalpara). Baikho pre-monsoon harvest festival. Dress names not yet sourced.

communities.name: Tea-garden (Adivasi) communities
communities.notes: Descendants of workers brought from central India in the 19th century. Red and white sarees popular among women; Jhumur dance. Show in varied roles, not only as plantation labour.

look_range.notes: Very wide range. Must not default Assam to a generic North Indian look or a generic East Asian look. Assam has no Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. Starting range, tune after test renders.

by_community.notes: Many people have East Asian facial features (Tibeto-Burman-speaking community).

adult_female.reason: The mekhela chador is the defining dress of Assamese women across religions (with the sador over the head for many Muslim women); golden muga silk, the Bodo dokhona and the Mising ege-gero are signature festive dresses.

adult_male.reason: Shirt and trousers or kurta-lungi with gamosa for everyday; dhoti, kurta and gamosa, or the Mising mibu galuk, for festivals.

child_boy.reason: Boys wear dhoti, kurta and gamosa at Bihu.

naming.notes: Given name, or given name plus father's name. Common Assamese surnames (e.g. Das, Gogoi, Saikia, Bora) mark caste or Ahom clan titles; never used.
Bodo clan surnames (e.g. Basumatary, Narzary) are community, not caste, names.

Confirmed by Wikipedia: Bodo dokhona (chest-to-ankle wrap) and aronai scarf; Mising ege and mibu galuk; Bwisagu in mid-April; Ali-Aye-Ligang starts on the first Wednesday of February (date made precise).
Corrected: Baikho date narrowed from 'pre-monsoon (around June)' to June, confirmed by EastMojo, Sentinel and India Today NE reports of 2023-2026.

Open: Wikipedia calls the Mising 'gadu' a blanket, while the Ministry of Culture's NVLI page describes a 'gadu galuk' jacket; kept as NVLI describes (the jacket), to be confirmed by a Mising reviewer. Aronai: Wikipedia describes a decorative scarf for special occasions; its use as an honour scarf comes from the Chirang district page only. Green Bodo gamsa is single-source (Chirang district).
